# Project mode in the skills, and the user docs for multi-repo runs ## What to build The engine and graph-manager now support multi-repo runs (spec goals MR-03 and the "Docs" requirements of `docs/prd/multi-repo.md`). This task teaches the three bundled skills (`to-spec`, `to-tasks`, `run-graph`) a **project mode** and documents the feature for users. It touches only Markdown skill files, their test, and the two READMEs; no TypeScript outside `packages/graph-execution/src/install/skills.test.ts`. What already exists in the code (from the tasks this one depends on), so the docs describe it exactly: - Engine: `graph-execution suite --project --provider [--concurrency n] [--model m] [--no-merge] [--human-review|--no-human-review] [--reviewers ] [--web]`. `--project` and `--feature` exclude each other. `` is a git repo holding `project.json` (`{ "name": "billing", "repos": [{ "name": "api", "path": "repos/api" }, …] }`, at least 2 repos, names `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, paths relative to the project folder or absolute), `contract.md` (required), `specs/.md` and `tasks//` per changed repo, optional `test-plan.json`. Code: `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/project.ts` (`PROJECT_FILE`, `loadProject`). - Each repo with a `tasks//` folder becomes a feature run in that repo, with that repo's `graph-execution.config.json`, and its spec is `specs/.md` + `## Contract` + `contract.md`. There is no merge step. Then the joint phase runs in `.graph-execution/suite-/worktrees/joint/` (one worktree per repo at `repos//` on `suite/`): every repo's validation commands, every enabled reviewer on the combined diff (paths prefixed `/`), the tester on `test-plan.json` (commands run from the joint folder, repos at `repos/`), and a fixer that may edit any repo. All or nothing: nothing is applied while a feature is failed; before the first apply every repo is checked (clean, same branch, same commit) and if one fails nothing is applied and every result stays on `suite/`. - Suites (single-repo and multi-repo) now take `--reviewers ` or `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS`, copy it to `.graph-execution/suite-/reviewers.json`, pass it to every feature run and use it in the e2e or joint phase. - graph-manager: a **Projects** page (a project = named group of workspaces from one forge, folder `/.projects//` with `repos/` links), agent terminals on a project (cwd = the project folder, env `GM_PROJECT_ID`), the project's Start run drawer (opened by `open_start_run` from a project terminal, with `project: true`), project runs in the Runs list with a project chip, sandboxed project runs, and **Create PR** opening one linked PR per changed repo with `docs/prd/done/.md` and `docs/prd/done/-contract.md`. ## Context: files to read before implementing - `docs/prd/multi-repo.md` — the whole spec; the "Skills (MR-03)" and "Docs" sections are this task's contract. - `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-spec/SKILL.md` (41 lines) — sections 1–4; add the project mode. - `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (229 lines) — "One PRD or several", step 5 (writing files), step 6 (validation), and the final "start the run" bullets. - `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (85 lines) — sections 1, 2, 5 and 6. - `.claude/skills/{to-spec,to-tasks,run-graph}/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/{to-tasks,run-graph}/SKILL.md` — repo copies of the bundled skills (`.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` is byte-identical to the bundled one today). Ignore the stray `SKILL 2.md`, `SKILL 3.md`, `validate-tasks 2.mjs`, `validate-tasks 3.mjs` files; do not edit or delete them. - `packages/graph-execution/src/install/skills.test.ts` (lines 100–140, `describe("the bundled skill")`) — string assertions on the bundled skills; add yours here. - `packages/graph-execution/README.md` — line ~41 (table of contents), ~91–92 (the `suite` usage lines), ~118 (`suite ...` row), ~350 (the sentence "Suites keep the built-in reviewers."), ~499–541 (the `## Suites` section), ~590–610 (skills section mentioning several PRDs and `run-graph`). - `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — `## The app` (~line 257), `### Agents and tools` (~268), `### Reviewers` (~287). ## Patterns to follow **Skill wording:** short imperative bullets, bold lead words, commands in fenced `bash` blocks, the same voice as the existing skills. For example, the existing suite bullet in `run-graph`: ``` - **Suite:** several features, each a task folder with its own PRD. Use it when `to-tasks` wrote several feature folders … ``` **Test pattern** (`skills.test.ts:109-116`): ```ts it("to-tasks and run-graph hand the run to graph-manager with open_start_run when it is available", async () => { for (const name of ["to-tasks", "run-graph"]) { const skill = await readFile(path.join(root, "skills", name, "SKILL.md"), "utf8"); expect(skill).toContain("open_start_run"); } }); ``` **README style:** the existing `## Suites` section: a command block, one-sentence intro, bold-led bullets, then a file tree of what it produces. ## Step-by-step tasks ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-spec/SKILL.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: a `## Project mode` section (before "### 4. Next" or as a sub-section of step 2): when the cwd holds `project.json` (a graph-manager project or a hand-made one), read `project.json` and each repo under `repos//`; write `contract.md` first (the APIs, schemas, messages or files shared between the repos, with exact shapes), then `specs/.md` for every repo that changes, each with the usual sections and its own Mermaid diagram; do not write in `docs/prd/`; ask the user to approve the contract and all specs together. Commit in the project folder's own git repo, never in the repos. - **GOTCHA**: keep the existing strings the test checks (`docs/prd/.md`, ```` ```mermaid ````, `docs/prd/done/`, `Do not continue until the user approves`). ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: add **Project** as a third case under "One PRD or several": the cwd holds `project.json`; each changed repo is a feature with its task folder at `tasks//` (not `.agents/tasks/`), written from `specs/.md` + `contract.md`; tasks of one repo never depend on another repo's tasks and file paths in task text are relative to that repo's root; write one joint `test-plan.json` at the project root whose steps run from the project root and reach repos through `repos/` (for example `cd repos/api && npm start`), checking that the repos work together; the repo's own checks go in `tasks//test-plan.json`. Validation: run `validate-tasks.mjs tasks/` once per task folder; the joint `test-plan.json` is checked by `graph-execution suite --project .` at start. Final step: in graph-manager call `open_start_run` with `project: true`; elsewhere show `graph-execution suite --project . --provider

--web`. Commit in the project folder's repo. - **GOTCHA**: keep `.agents/tasks/.json`, `validate-tasks.mjs .agents/tasks`, `open_start_run`, "`graph-manager` MCP server" and `**Start run**` (asserted by the test); no "HITL"/"AFK". ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: section 1 gains **Project**: the cwd holds `project.json`. Section 5: `graph-execution suite --project . --provider

--web` (from the project folder), or `open_start_run` with `project: true` in graph-manager; `--sandbox` works for projects too in graph-manager. Section 6, for a project suite: one box per repo, no merge nodes, then the **Joint review** (each repo's validation, reviewers on the combined diff with `/` paths, the tester on the joint test plan, a fixer for any repo); nothing is applied until everything passes; then every repo gets its changes as uncommitted changes; in graph-manager, **Create PR** opens one linked PR per repo. Update the `description:` frontmatter to also mention a multi-repo project, keeping it starting with `Start a graph-execution run`. ### UPDATE the repo copies - **IMPLEMENT**: copy the three updated bundled files over `.claude/skills/to-spec/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md`, and the to-tasks/run-graph ones over `.agents/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (`cp`), so the repo's own agents use the same text. ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/install/skills.test.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: one new `it("the skills have a project mode for multi-repo runs", …)` in `describe("the bundled skill")`: every one of the three skills contains `project.json`; `to-spec` contains `contract.md` and `specs/.md`; `to-tasks` contains `tasks//` and `repos/`; `run-graph` and `to-tasks` contain `suite --project .`. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- install/skills` ### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/README.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: usage line `graph-execution suite --project

--provider [...]` next to the `--feature` one, and `[--reviewers ]` on both; a `### Multi-repo suites` subsection at the end of `## Suites` (before "What a suite produces" or after it) with: the command, the project folder layout as a tree, a `project.json` example, what runs where (feature runs in their repos with their configs, spec + contract), the joint phase, all or nothing incl. the pre-apply check, what it produces (`.graph-execution/suite-/specs/`, `joint/spec.md`, `worktrees/joint/repos//`, `suite/` in every repo), and `list`/`clean`/`open`/`--resume` behaviour; replace "Suites keep the built-in reviewers." (~line 350) with a sentence that suites use the reviewers file too (copied to `suite-/reviewers.json`, passed to every feature run and used in the e2e or joint phase); add the multi-repo link to the table of contents line ~41 if the TOC lists subsections (it lists only top-level sections; then skip); mention project mode in the skills section (~590–610). ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md` - **IMPLEMENT**: under `## The app`, a `### Projects` subsection: what a project is (named workspaces from one forge), where its folder lives (`/.projects//`, a local git repo with `repos/` links, never pushed), opening an agent on a project, the project's Start run, project runs on the Runs page, sandboxes, and **Create PR** (one PR per changed repo, linked, with `docs/prd/done/.md` and `-contract.md`). Under `### Reviewers`, say that reviewers now also run in suites and project runs. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The three bundled skills describe project mode; the repo copies in `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` match the bundled files byte for byte (`cmp` exits 0). - [ ] `skills.test.ts` has the new project-mode test and every test in it passes. - [ ] The engine README documents `suite --project`, `project.json`, the layout, the joint phase, all or nothing and `--reviewers` for suites, and no longer says suites keep the built-in reviewers. - [ ] The graph-manager README has a `### Projects` subsection. - [ ] No TypeScript other than `skills.test.ts` changed. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-execution -- install/skills cmp packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md .claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md cmp packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md .agents/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md grep -n "built-in reviewers" packages/graph-execution/README.md # must not print "Suites keep the built-in reviewers" ```
